title: Sparse Autoencoder Feature Stability Under Fine-Tuning: Do Safety Features Survive Safety-Irrelevant Fine-Tuning?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: demonstrating that safety features are disproportionately fragile to fine-tuning would explain safety degradation and motivate feature-stable fine-tuning techniques, but the chain to a concrete solution is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires training SAEs, fine-tuning a model on a downstream task, retraining or transferring SAEs, and measuring feature-level stability. This multi-stage pipeline with both SAE training and model fine-tuning is advanced for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: SAE training on base model, model fine-tuning, re-SAE training, feature stability measurement, safety/capability feature comparison, and correlation with benchmark changes. Many sequential stages.

novelty.reasoning: While it is well-established that fine-tuning compromises safety alignment ('Fine-Tuning Aligned Language Models Compromises Safety', ICLR 2024), and sparse crosscoders exist for comparing model versions, the specific SAE-level feature stability measurement — training SAEs before and after safety-irrelevant fine-tuning and measuring whether safety features are disproportionately fragile — has not been directly conducted. Safe-SAIL (arXiv:2509.18127) maps safety features but does not study their stability under fine-tuning. The SAE feature transferability work (EMNLP 2025) studied cross-model transfer but not within-model fine-tuning stability. This is a novel experimental design with practical implications for understanding safety degradation.

evidence: Qi et al. (2024). Fine-Tuning Aligned Language Models Compromises Safety, Even When Users Do Not Intend To. ICLR 2024.
